name: Fog of War Reveal
description: Two maps, not one: what you can see now, and what you have ever seen. world.vision_system computes current line of sight and owns the live layer; this component listens to its updates and accumulates the history layer — the dimmed, remembered geography that lets a player plan the route back. Keeping history out of the vision system matters because sight is per-frame and ephemeral while memory is per-save and persistent; conflating them is how fog ends up resetting every time the player blinks. This component owns recording and reveal queries only: rendering the two layers is a presentation concern, and persistence.save_system snapshots the history like any other state.

inputs.name: revealRadiusBonus
inputs.description: Extra tiles of history recorded beyond live sight. Zero means you remember exactly what you saw; a bonus forgives camera edge cases.

inputs.name: rememberEntities
inputs.description: Whether revealed enemies stay marked on the history layer. False records terrain only — the honest default, since a remembered enemy that moved is a lie on the map.

inputs.name: persistBetweenFloors
inputs.description: Whether history survives world.floor_descent transitions. False: every floor starts unknown. True is for single-dungeon games where the map is the progression.

outputs.name: exploredTileCount
outputs.description: Tiles ever revealed on this floor.

outputs.name: exploredFraction
outputs.description: 0..1 of the floor's walkable tiles revealed — the completionist metric.
